from_statement: AUTHOR PROOF; INDEPENDENT REVIEW PENDING. Let B_n be n by n with mutually independent uniform {-1,1} entries. Let E_n mean that some two rows or some two columns agree up to sign. The probability E_n of any projective row or column collision equals 1-2^(-(n-1)^2) sum_{a,b=1}^n s(n,a)s(n,b)2^((a-1)(b-1)), where s are signed Stirling numbers of the first kind.

from_statement: AUTHOR PROOF; INDEPENDENT REVIEW PENDING. Let B_n be n by n with mutually independent uniform {-1,1} entries. Let E_n mean that some two rows or some two columns agree up to sign. With A=binom(n,2), m=2^(n-1), 2A/m-(3A^2-A)/m^2 <= P(E_n) <= 2A/m. Hence P(E_n)=(2+o(1))n(n-1)2^-n and no fixed K makes epsilon+K2^-n an upper bound for the full least-singular-value tail for all n,epsilon.

from_statement: AUTHOR PROOF; INDEPENDENT REVIEW PENDING. Let B_n be n by n with mutually independent uniform {-1,1} entries. Let E_n mean that some two rows or some two columns agree up to sign. to_statement: For a sign matrix B_n, E_n means that some two distinct rows or some two distinct columns agree up to a global sign. E_n implies singularity by a left or right kernel vector supported on two coordinates. The converse is false; E_n is a specified subset of singularity, not all singularity.

from_statement: AUTHOR PROOF; INDEPENDENT REVIEW PENDING. For every n>=5 there exists a real {-1,1} matrix of rank n-1, with no +/- equal row or column pair, and with both left and right two-coordinate restricted least singular values at least sqrt(2).
to_statement: The proposed universal bridge is: every singular real sign matrix has a left or right nonzero kernel vector supported on at most two coordinates. This bridge is false even for corank-one matrices of every dimension n>=5. A counterexample to this bridge is not a refutation of the Spielman-Teng conjecture.

from_statement: For G_1=[Z] with Z standard normal, P(s_min(G_1)<=t)=erf(t/sqrt(2)) for t>=0; its derivative at zero is sqrt(2/pi). Thus 1-exp(-t-t^2/2) is not the exact finite-n Gaussian least-singular-value CDF. It is the limiting CDF as n tends to infinity (Rudelson-Vershynin ICM 2010 survey). The finite-n bound P(s_min(G_n)<=t/sqrt(n))<=t is a separate statement. This corrects only the exact-law sentence in the 2026-09-07 C0029 attempt record.
